title: Capacity Playbook — GPU-hour burn and $/1M token costs by region
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working sheet is a playbook-style reference for sizing Redwood's inference capacity across regions and GPU families. It focuses on two outputs teams commonly ask for: (1) expected GPU-hour burn by workload tier and region, and (2) normalized $/1M tokens cost after accounting for utilization, batching, caching, and instance pricing (on-demand / reserved / spot). Goal is to provide a repeatable set of assumptions and quick sensitivity knobs for planning Dedicated capacity and Dedicated pricing conversations.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Using conservative throughput and utilization assumptions, a mid-sized tenant (100 qps sustained, 50k avg tokens/day) maps to ~X-200 GPU-hours/day on H100-equivalent hardware at 65% effective utilization. After layering region-specific VM pricing, network egress, and a 12% ops overhead, estimated baseline $/1M tokens ranges from $9.2 (us-central) to $14.8 (europe-west1) on reserved contracts; spot-optimized mixes can reduce compute line by ~20–30% but add preemption risk and additional replication/headroom cost.

Key assumptions (use these when reproducing the spreadsheet):
- GPU types considered: NVIDIA H100 (80GB), A100-40GB, L4 (inference-optimized).
- Baseline per-GPU sustained token throughput (steady-state conversational workload, mixed seq length): H100=350k tokens/min, A100=210k tokens/min, L4=95k tokens/min. These are conservative vs peak kernels to model real-world multi-tenant interference.
- Effective utilization = scheduled usage * packing efficiency. Typical packing efficiency = 0.75 for bursty web traffic with dynamic batching. Scheduled usage baseline = 0.85 for Dedicated pools with autoscale smoothing. Combined effective util baseline = 0.64.
- Average sequence length (tokens/request) scenarios: short=32, mid=128, long=512. Token mix used in scenarios below.
- Pricing buckets per region (example blended on-reserved hourly): us-west1: H100=$18/hr, A100=$8.6/hr, L4=$2.1/hr. europe-west1: +20% to compute. ap-southeast1: +30% to compute. Spot discounts assumed: H100 ~60% off reserved, A100 ~50% off, L4 ~40% off (region dependent).
- Network egress: $0.02 per GiB local inter-az, $0.08 per GiB inter-region (applies for cross-region fallbacks).
- Storage and image overhead: $0.12/hr/GPU amortized (state, logs, checkpoint storage).
- Ops & license overhead: 12% of compute+storage.

Primary sheet sections (format reference for copy into a spreadsheet):
1) Region x GPU inventory table (columns): region, gpu_type, list_price/hr, reserved_blended/hr, spot_blended/hr, available_az, typical_provision_latency_hrs.
2) Throughput & utilization (columns): gpu_type, tokens_per_min_peak, tokens_per_min_sustained, packing_eff, scheduled_util, effective_util, tokens_per_gpu_per_hr_effective.
3) Scenario matrix (rows): scenario_name, token_mix(short/mid/long %), qps_profile (avg/spike), daily_token_demand, required_gpu_hours/day (H100-equivalent), recommended_pool_margin(%), suggested_provision(model type & purchase mix).
4) Normalized cost breakdown ($/1M tokens) (columns): region, gpu_compute, storage_amort, network, ops_overhead, fallback_capacity, total_cost, effective_cost_after_caching.

Representative scenario outputs (examples trimmed for doc):
- Scenario A (PLG web chat, mid seq mix): token_mix=10/70/20 (short/mid/long), daily_tokens=50M. Using H100 baseline: tokens per GPU per day (effective) = 350k/min * 60 * 24 * effective_util (0.64) = ~19.2M tokens/day per GPU. Required GPUs ~= 50M / 19.2M = 2.6 -> round to 3 with 20% margin => 3.6 GPUs -> 86 GPU-hours/day.
  Cost (us-west1, reserved H100 blend): compute = 86 * $18 = $1548/day. Storage amort + ops + network ~ $230/day. Normalized => $34 / 1M tokens (this is a high-availability, reserved-only no-spot scenario).
- Scenario B (SaaS customer heavy embedding + batch queries): token_mix=40/50/10, aggregated batch jobs reduce packing inefficiencies; packing_eff=0.9, scheduled_util=0.75 => effective_util=0.675. Daily_tokens=150M. H100 tokens/day effective ~= 20.7M => required GPUs = 7.25 => 9 GPUs with 25% margin = 216 GPU-hrs/day. Mix reserved:spot (60:40) assumed; compute cost blend reduces compute line to ~$2,700/day. Normalized => $10.8 / 1M tokens.

Sensitivity knobs (quick change impacts to $/1M tokens):
- Utilization +/- 10pp -> ~ +/- 14% change to compute line.
- Packing efficiency delta 0.6 -> 0.85 changes cost ~ +/-18% (largest single runtime lever).
- Spot percentage: moving from 0% to 40% spot reduces compute by ~20–28% depending on region & GPU. But add 8–12% excess capacity to cover preemption windows and warmup.
- Region premium: europe +20% compute -> linear bump in $/1M tokens; cross-region egress for failover adds non-linear tail costs for low-frequency failovers.

Operational playbook summary (practical guidance):
- Start Dedicated sizing conversations with the scenario matrix (section 3) generating a baseline reserved capacity. Add a small spot pool and an autoscale cold-pool for spike absorb.
- For enterprise customers needing consistent latency guarantees, price to reserved-only baseline, include a 15–20% premium for SLA+redundancy.
- For PLG customers with elastic patterns, run a spot-optimized profile and provide recommended headroom (15% over steady-state).
- Maintain a regional emergency cushion: 10% of committed capacity in region as hot standby, and 20–30% cross-region failover buffer (only charge to customers on failover).

What to track in the spreadsheet/console (metrics to export weekly):
- Per-region GPU utilization (scheduled vs effective), average batch size, requests per second percentiles (p50/p95/p99), preemption events (spot), cold-start times for scaling, egress volume per failover event, token mix drift per tenant.

Open questions / TODOs in this draft:
- Re-run microbenchmarks for L4 family with our current kernel stack (post-quantization), prior numbers are from vendor guidance and need lab verification.
- Integrate real Reserved pricing tiers for 1yr vs 3yr discounts into region table (currently using 1yr blended).
- Model caching impact more explicitly: prefix-KV cache hit rates change token accounting non-linearly; need a small Monte Carlo to show distribution.
- Add a column for amortized model load cost (large model warmups cause transient token backlogs).

Appendix: quick formulas to port into a spreadsheet:
- tokens_per_gpu_per_hr_effective = tokens_per_min_sustained * 60 * effective_util
- required_gpu_hours_day = ceil((daily_tokens / tokens_per_gpu_per_hr_effective) * (1 + margin_pct)) * 24? (note: prefer computing required GPUs then multiply by 24 for hours)
- $/1M_tokens = (daily_compute_cost + daily_storage + daily_network + ops_overhead + fallback_capacity_cost) / (daily_tokens / 1_000_000)

Suggested next steps for owners:
- Ops infra (Owen) run short perf sweep for L4/A100/H100 on 2026-03-05 and drop numbers into throughput sheet tab.
- Finance (Marco) add updated 3yr reserved pricing tiers and run blended cost scenarios for enterprise proposals.
- Product (Lena) validate recommended margin and SLA add-ons with Solutions Engs for the next Dedicated pitch.

Notes to self (working):
- This is intentionally a lean sheet — keep one tab for base assumptions and another for scenarios. Avoid copying multiple small per-tenant tabs; instead produce parameterized scenario templates.
- Link to benchmarking artifacts when results are in: CONFLUENCE-ENG-4321.

End of playbook draft.

(If pasting into Google Sheets: split the representative tables into separate tabs: regions, throughput, scenarios, cost-breakdown, sensitivity. Use the formulas in Appendix cells.)
